title: Day 758: Real Estate Salesman Shot Dead Inside Car in Culiacán's Las Cucas Neighborhood
detail: Avelino 'N', 58, a real estate salesman, was found dead on Thursday, August 20, 2026, inside a gray sedan parked with its front doors open in a residential garage at the intersection of Velina León de Medina and Alejandro Hernández Tyler streets in the Las Cucas neighborhood of Culiacán. Reports indicate he had come to visit a relative's home when armed individuals approached and shot him; the vehicle showed impacts from large-caliber rounds. No arrests were reported.

media.caption: Real estate salesman Avelino 'N' found shot dead inside a car in the Las Cucas neighborhood, Culiacán, August 20, 2026

title: Day 758: Five More Bodies Found Across Mazatlán in Single Day, Capping Region's Most Violent August
detail: The FGE opened five additional homicide investigation files for Mazatlán on Thursday, August 20, 2026, on top of the Culiacán case — the deadliest single day of the month for the port. A man, Manuel, approximately 27, was shot repeatedly by gunmen in a gray sedan at his home on Calle de las Cofradías in the Urbi Villas del Real subdivision and died at the scene. A body was found on the Culiacán–Mazatlán highway; others were located in the María Elena and Benito Juárez neighborhoods, and a fifth victim died of gunshot wounds sustained inside a residential property on Avenida Del Delfín. Five vehicle-theft reports and three forced-disappearance complaints were also filed the same day. August 2026 has become Mazatlán's most violent month on record, with roughly 40 homicides in the port so far.

media.caption: Young man shot dead inside a home in Urbi Villas del Real, Mazatlán, August 20, 2026

title: Day 758: Los Mochis Produce-Market President Abducted, Found Safe a Day Later
detail: José Pimentel Moncada, 61, president of the Central de Abastos ('La Yarda Grande') wholesale produce market in Los Mochis, Ahome, was forced into a vehicle by armed men in two vehicles around 3:00 PM on Thursday, August 20, 2026, as he left the market on Rosendo G. Castro street heading home. His children posted a video appealing for his safe return, describing him as a lifelong market, agriculture, and transport worker with no history of conflict. He was located safe and reunited with his family by August 21; Mexican outlets did not disclose the circumstances of his release.

media.caption: Family of José Pimentel Moncada, abducted president of the Los Mochis Central de Abastos, appeals for his safe return
